title: Process Highest-Priority Compression Tasks
real_world_story: A compression service receives multiple files waiting to be processed. Some files have higher processing priority than others, so the system must always select the highest-priority available task first.

real_world_connection.target_represents: The order in which tasks should be processed
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Repeatedly selecting the currently highest-priority task before processing the next task

problem_statement: Given N compression tasks, each with a task ID and priority, process the tasks in descending order of priority. If two tasks have the same priority, process the task with the smaller task ID first.
task: Determine the order in which the compression system should process all tasks using priority-based greedy processing.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N, the number of compression tasks. Each of the next N lines contains two integers: task ID and priority.
output_format: Print the task IDs in the order in which they should be processed, separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: Tasks 102 and 104 have the highest priority 5, so they are processed first. Task 102 has the smaller ID and is processed before 104.
Tasks with priority 10 are processed first, followed by priority 8 and then priority 7. For equal priority, the smaller task ID comes first.

expected_algorithm.name: Priority-style Greedy Processing
expected_algorithm.reason: The system can make the locally optimal choice at each step by selecting the highest-priority available compression task, with task ID used as the tie-breaker.

hint: Store each task together with its priority.
Always select the task with the highest priority.
When priorities are equal, select the smaller task ID.
A priority queue or sorting-based approach can efficiently determine the processing order.
real_world_takeaway: Priority-based greedy processing allows compression systems to handle important or urgent tasks first while efficiently managing a large number of pending operations.
